messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Actuator Bead-Based Chemiluminescent Immunoassay for Cardiac Marker Detection (cTnI / CK-MB / Myoglobin)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cardiac Sample (biological sample, e.g. whole blood, serum, or plasma, containing a cardiac marker such as cardiac troponin I, CK-MB, or myoglobin)
  - Capture Beads (magnetically responsive beads coated with primary capture antibody)
  - Blocking Antibody (blocking protein/antibody reagent)
  - Reporter Antibody (secondary reporter antibody)
  - Wash Buffer (droplet-based merge-and-split dilution wash buffer, 0.05M TRIS, 0.1 M NaCl, 0.1 mg/mL BSA, 0.02% Tween20, pH 9.5)
  - Chemiluminescent Substrate (detection substrate, e.g. APS-5)

STEPS:
1. Dispense a cardiac sample droplet, a capture-bead droplet, and a blocking-antibody droplet.
2. Mix the capture beads with the blocking antibody to form reagent 1.
3. Combine the sample droplet with reagent 1 to form the assay droplet; incubate at room temperature (~23C) for 3 minutes to allow capture antibody-antigen binding.
4. Execute a droplet-based wash step: merge the assay droplet with wash buffer and discard the resulting supernatant, removing unbound sample material.
5. Dispense a reporter-antibody droplet and merge it with the assay droplet; incubate 2 minutes at room temperature to form the capture-antibody-antigen-reporter-antibody complex.
6. Execute a droplet-based wash protocol (11 repeated merge-and-split dilution washes with wash buffer) to deplete unbound reporter antibody and antigen from the bead droplet.
7. Combine the washed bead droplet with chemiluminescent substrate; incubate ~2 minutes at 25C.
8. Detect the chemiluminescent signal for 5 seconds, indicative of the quantity of the cardiac marker in the biological sample.
9. If the measured signal exceeds the top-end of the standard curve, execute an auto-dilution sequence (merge with a diluent droplet, re-detect) to bring the concentration back within the linear range of detection.
10. Discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful cardiac marker quantification is confirmed by a calibration curve relating chemiluminescent response (counts/s) to marker concentration (ng/mL) for cTn-I, CK-MB, and myoglobin, with good linearity and recovery percentages clustered near 100% across the calibrator concentration range, and with total assay time (sample loading to detectable signal) of well under 5-10 minutes for multiplexed cardiac marker panels, supporting use of the platform for rapid triage of chest-pain patients and assessment of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) risk.

module chemiluminescence

manifest CardiacSample
manifest CaptureBeads
manifest BlockingAntibody
manifest ReporterAntibody
manifest WashBuffer
manifest ChemiluminescentSubstrate

instructions:

sample = dispense 20 units of CardiacSample
beads = dispense 40 units of CaptureBeads
blocker = dispense 40 units of BlockingAntibody

reagent1 = mix beads with blocker

assay = mix sample with reagent1 for 60s
heat assay at 23c for 3m

wash1 = dispense 40 units of WashBuffer
washed1 = mix assay with wash1 for 30s
dispose washed1

reporter = dispense 40 units of ReporterAntibody
assay2 = mix assay with reporter for 60s
heat assay2 at 23c for 2m

repeat 11 times {
    washbuf = dispense 40 units of WashBuffer
    assay2 = mix assay2 with washbuf for 30s
}

substrate = dispense 20 units of ChemiluminescentSubstrate
detection_droplet = mix assay2 with substrate for 30s
heat detection_droplet at 25c for 2m

cardiac_marker_signal = detect chemiluminescence on detection_droplet for 5s

if (cardiac_marker_signal > 120000) {
    diluent = dispense 20 units of WashBuffer
    diluted_droplet = mix detection_droplet with diluent for 30s
    diluted_signal = detect chemiluminescence on diluted_droplet for 5s
    dispose diluted_droplet
}

dispose detection_droplet

metadata.protocol_name: Detection of Cardiac Markers on a Droplet Actuator (Sista et al., US8,846,414 B2)

sources.title: Detection of Cardiac Markers on a Droplet Actuator
sources.publisher: Picoliter / US Patent US8,846,414 B2, Advanced Liquid Logic, Inc. and Duke University

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the patent's droplet-actuator immunoassay protocol (Sections 7.7 Immunoassays and 7.8.3 Assay Protocol, Fig. 3A-3E, and claim 24), covering bead+blocking-antibody reagent formation, sample binding incubation, first wash, reporter-antibody addition and second incubation, the repeated merge-and-split wash protocol (Section 7.6 Bead Washing), substrate combination and chemiluminescent detection, and the claim-55 auto-dilution branch for out-of-range signals. Incubation times/temperatures, wash-repeat count (11 washes), and detection duration (5s) are taken directly from Section 7.8.3's described assay protocol. Because BioScript's dispense grammar accepts only integer unit counts, the patent's stated microliter volumes (2.2 uL sample, 4.2 uL reagent aliquots) are approximated as whole-number unit counts (20, 40) rather than reproduced exactly.

numeric_mismatches.note: BioScript's dispense grammar requires integer unit literals only. The patent's actual stated volumes are fractional microliters (2.2 uL sample, 4.2 uL reagent aliquots, 4.4 uL wash droplets); whole-number unit counts (20, 40) are used as a proportional approximation rather than the exact stated volumes.

The numeric threshold is not stated verbatim as a cutoff value in the patent; it is approximated from the response-count (counts/s) scale shown in the calibration-curve figures (Fig. 6A cTn-I, Fig. 7A CK-MB, Fig. 8A myoglobin), which range up to roughly 1.3-1.6e5 counts/s at the top calibrator concentration.

The patent's Section 7.8.3 states the APS-5 chemiluminescent substrate is merged with the bead droplet and detection performed for 5 seconds, but does not specify a separate pre-detection incubation temperature/duration for the substrate-bead mixture; a short 25C/2-minute incubation is included as a reasonable modeling step before the detect call, not a value taken verbatim from the text.
